bull_bear.body:
- **No dividend / buyback / capital return** — "there is none so far."
- Board policy: deploy cash pile into "businesses of tomorrow" — core print (copy-share) + Digital (incl. Digicontent).
- AFE: non-cash acquisitions; active divestiture to maximize value, "not desperate sellers."
- Treasury = "patient capital," will ride out the yield curve (no forced sales despite MTM losses).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Newsprint cost inflation + INR depreciation squeezing print margin.
- Ad-yield sustainability vs competitive reaction (pricing not guaranteed structural).
- Radio sector "under a lot of pressure" structurally; remaining stations need profit growth.
- Treasury MTM exposure to rising bond yields (already −INR 50 cr other income hit).
- Statutory/labour-code provisions could bring further exceptional items.
- Large cash pile with no return policy = capital-allocation / value-trap concern raised by analysts.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and reform-minded; multiple analysts congratulated mgmt for "finally" shutting unviable OTTplay & Radio frequencies ("better late than never"). CFO upbeat on print pricing ("played out beautifully"), candid that OTTplay "didn't work" despite Tier-2/3 distribution strategy and telco competition. Repeatedly deflected forward guidance. Defensive on cash return.
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- HMVL "other operating income" spike (~+100% YoY, ~INR 32 cr) is **AFE forfeiture** revenue — non-recurring quality of earnings flag.
- Other income drop (−INR 50 cr) is **MTM treasury losses**, not operational — should reverse if yields fall.
- OTTplay intersegment reversal restated HMVL PY print revenue down INR 6 cr (accounting, non-operational).
- Group's real digital growth vehicle is **Digicontent Ltd**, sitting *outside* the listed HT Media consol — optionality not visible in HTML numbers.
- Assetvault/AasaanWill is an unrelated-looking estate/will-planning AFE bet (8+ yrs, ~nil revenue) — speculative.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- "the Board approved a preferential issue last month, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval. The proposed issue is a proactive step towards strengthening the Company's capital structure, streamlining its debt profile and providing capital for general business requirements." The deck does not disclose issue size, price or subscriber.
- Balance-sheet position is presented as a strength: "Cash position remains robust", with Net Cash (defined as "Balance at the end of the period") of INR 922 crore at Q1FY27 versus INR 1,001 crore at Q4FY26 and INR 976 crore at Q1FY26.
- No dividend, buyback or capex-funding policy is discussed anywhere in the deck.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Radio segment structural decline — Radio continues to face growth uncertainty driven by profitability challenges and shifting audience tastes, with muted growth from subdued advertiser sentiment and continued pressure on advertising rates.
- Print circulation decline — Print media faces continued circulation pressures even as advertising shows early signs of recovery, reflecting a structural shift in reader consumption away from the medium.
- Newsprint cost and input volatility — Rising newsprint costs, exacerbated by a weakening rupee and global supply chain disruption, are a recurring pressure the Company must manage through procurement strategy.
- Digital-driven ad budget reallocation — Advertising budgets are increasingly reallocated toward digital platforms as Digital media has surpassed TV in share, structurally pressuring traditional Print and Radio ad revenue.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical volatility affecting input costs — Geopolitical tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and global trade fragmentation have increased volatility in commodity markets, with crude oil price pressure flowing through to petrol, diesel and gas costs relevant to the Company's cost base and consumer spending environment.

outlook.body:
- **No formal forward revenue/earnings guidance** (stated policy).
- **No further exceptional / discontinued-ops losses expected** from business cleanup — explicit "simple answer is no" — EXCEPT potential statutory impact from new labour codes if anything further arises.
- OTTplay wind-down: only **"very small"/marginal P&L residual** in FY27 (servicing pre-31-Mar subscriptions, 1–6 month tails to ~Sep); but **cash outflow** to exit content/ISP/channel-partner contracts.
- Ad yields: management "hopes & plans" to hold deal pricing "at a certain level and above, not below" — sustainability caveated by competitive reaction.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body: - AFE (Advertising-For-Equity / barter) portfolio: mix of fully-matured, semi-matured and "under-baked" assets; actively monetized opportunistically ("active sellers, not desperate sellers"). New AFE acquisitions are **non-cash** (paid in ad space). New AFE bet: **Assetvault Ltd (brand "AasaanWill")** — INR 22 cr non-cash AFE investment, near-nil revenue so far.
outlook.title: Pipeline / order book

outlook.body:
- Pricing power in print ad yields ("played out very beautifully this quarter") — key swing factor; structural durability uncertain.
- Copy-share strategy = long-term reader base / advertiser value chain ("recruit new readers → value prop to advertisers → AFE onboarding → pricing").
- AFE asset monetization track record (4–5 yrs) as recurring cash-flow optionality.
- >INR 1,000 cr cash optionality for "businesses of tomorrow" / Digital.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue to invest selectively in scalable digital opportunities while remaining committed to core Print, Radio and Digital businesses.
- Embed AI capabilities across editorial, operational and recruitment workflows, and refine the data and technology stack organisation-wide.
- In Radio, shift strategic focus toward expanding non-FCT (Non-Free Commercial Time) revenue streams via the events and experiential economy, strengthen high-potential stations, deepen local audience relevance, and rationalise the network footprint by exiting persistently underperforming stations.
- In Digital, pursue a sharper, more disciplined portfolio strategy prioritising businesses with clearer paths to scale, differentiation and profitability; concentrate resources on digital offerings better aligned with consumer behaviour and monetisation potential.
- In Print, sustain advertising-led growth on flagship English and Hindi mastheads through innovation-led advertising solutions, circulation enhancement initiatives and reader engagement efforts.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
- India's Media & Entertainment sector is expected to grow at a moderate 2.8% to reach INR 2.86 trillion, with advertising remaining the key growth driver even as Digital media and Live Events growth moderates and Print/Radio stay sluggish.
- Print advertising revenues are projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 2% through CY 2028E on continued effectiveness in reaching affluent consumers, while circulation revenues face a gradual decline.
- Radio advertisement revenues are expected to contract at a 2% CAGR through CY 2028E as FM receivers become less common in cars and phones, though a robust 14% growth in alternate revenues (content production, agency services, influencer marketing) is expected to offset losses.
- Digital advertising is expected to remain the primary growth engine for the industry as both large enterprises and SMEs increasingly invest in high-attribution formats.
- Rising newsprint costs, exacerbated by a weakening rupee and global supply chain disruption, are being managed through procurement discipline and a calibrated input-mix strategy; management will continue to watch how these pressures evolve.
- Radio's growth outlook remains uncertain, driven by profitability challenges and shifting audience tastes, despite the segment now deriving about 25% of revenue from non-FCT streams.
- Events have emerged as an incremental growth lever, contributing approximately 4%-6% to overall Print segment revenues.
- Central government advertisement rate increases, AI-driven creative solutions adoption, and continued growth in event-based revenues are cited as incremental supports to Print segment performance in the coming year.

- Hindustan Media Ventures Limited — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary since 01-Jul-03; extent of shareholding 74.40%
- HT Music and Entertainment Company Limited — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary since 28-Oct-05; extent of shareholding 100.00%
- HT Overseas Pte. Ltd. — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary since 19-Aug-10; foreign subsidiary reporting in Singapore Dollars; extent of shareholding 100.00%
- Next Mediaworks Limited — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary since 15-Apr-19; extent of shareholding 100.00%
- Next Radio Limited — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary since 15-Apr-19; became a direct (rather than step-down) subsidiary w.e.f. Feb 7, 2025 after loan-to-equity conversion; extent of shareholding 51.00% (effective holding including indirect stake via Next Mediaworks is higher)
- HT Noida (Company) Limited — subsidiary: Indirect subsidiary since 11-Feb-20, held through Hindustan Media Ventures Limited; extent of shareholding 100.00%
- Mosaic Media Ventures Private Limited — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary since 02-Dec-20; extent of shareholding 100.00%
- HT Content Studio LLP — JV: Former joint venture (held via Hindustan Media Ventures Limited); struck off by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs effective September 8, 2025, ceasing to be a JV
- Earthstone Holding (Two) Private Limited — related party: Holding company with direct or indirect control over the Company; ultimate controlling party is the Promoter Group
- The Hindustan Times Limited — related party: Holding Company of HT Media Limited
- Digicontent Limited — related party: Fellow subsidiary with whom transactions occurred during the year
- HT Digital Streams Limited — related party: Fellow subsidiary with whom transactions occurred during the year

segment_detail.title: Segment detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Print** is the clear engine — growth led by **yields/pricing**, volumes broadly flat (tracking industry). Conscious **copy-share** investment in key markets (English circ copies +13% in Q4), financed by ad-yield gains; realization per copy up only marginally (competition-constrained).
- **Radio** under structural sector pressure; high event-led base in PY hurt YoY; network footprint sharpened by surrendering 6 loss-making frequencies — all remaining frequencies now profitable.
- **Digital** reset: OTTplay shut; remaining Shine + Mosaic roughly breakeven-negative, flat revenue. Group digital ambitions sit largely in **Digicontent Ltd** (outside HTML consol).

order_book.title: Pipeline / order book
order_book.body: - AFE (Advertising-For-Equity / barter) portfolio: mix of fully-matured, semi-matured and "under-baked" assets; actively monetized opportunistically ("active sellers, not desperate sellers"). New AFE acquisitions are **non-cash** (paid in ad space). New AFE bet: **Assetvault Ltd (brand "AasaanWill")** — INR 22 cr non-cash AFE investment, near-nil revenue so far.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **No formal forward revenue/earnings guidance** (stated policy).
- **No further exceptional / discontinued-ops losses expected** from business cleanup — explicit "simple answer is no" — EXCEPT potential statutory impact from new labour codes if anything further arises.
- OTTplay wind-down: only **"very small"/marginal P&L residual** in FY27 (servicing pre-31-Mar subscriptions, 1–6 month tails to ~Sep); but **cash outflow** to exit content/ISP/channel-partner contracts.
- Ad yields: management "hopes & plans" to hold deal pricing "at a certain level and above, not below" — sustainability caveated by competitive reaction.

growth_optionality.title: Growth / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- Pricing power in print ad yields ("played out very beautifully this quarter") — key swing factor; structural durability uncertain.
- Copy-share strategy = long-term reader base / advertiser value chain ("recruit new readers → value prop to advertisers → AFE onboarding → pricing").
- AFE asset monetization track record (4–5 yrs) as recurring cash-flow optionality.
- >INR 1,000 cr cash optionality for "businesses of tomorrow" / Digital.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's Media & Entertainment sector is expected to grow at a moderate 2.8% to reach INR 2.86 trillion, with advertising remaining the key growth driver even as Digital media and Live Events growth moderates and Print/Radio stay sluggish.
- Print advertising revenues are projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 2% through CY 2028E on continued effectiveness in reaching affluent consumers, while circulation revenues face a gradual decline.
- Radio advertisement revenues are expected to contract at a 2% CAGR through CY 2028E as FM receivers become less common in cars and phones, though a robust 14% growth in alternate revenues (content production, agency services, influencer marketing) is expected to offset losses.
- Digital advertising is expected to remain the primary growth engine for the industry as both large enterprises and SMEs increasingly invest in high-attribution formats.
- Rising newsprint costs, exacerbated by a weakening rupee and global supply chain disruption, are being managed through procurement discipline and a calibrated input-mix strategy; management will continue to watch how these pressures evolve.
- Radio's growth outlook remains uncertain, driven by profitability challenges and shifting audience tastes, despite the segment now deriving about 25% of revenue from non-FCT streams.
- Events have emerged as an incremental growth lever, contributing approximately 4%-6% to overall Print segment revenues.
- Central government advertisement rate increases, AI-driven creative solutions adoption, and continued growth in event-based revenues are cited as incremental supports to Print segment performance in the coming year.

margins.title: Margins & cost (newsprint)
margins.body:
- EBITDA margin +100 bps YoY (consol and Print). 
- **Key headwind: rising newsprint costs**, amplified by a **weakening rupee** and global supply-chain / trade-policy / geopolitical disruption — flagged by Chairperson as the near-term concern, managed via "cost discipline."
- Radio margin negative; loss reduced via frequency surrenders.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- **No dividend / buyback / capital return** — "there is none so far."
- Board policy: deploy cash pile into "businesses of tomorrow" — core print (copy-share) + Digital (incl. Digicontent).
- AFE: non-cash acquisitions; active divestiture to maximize value, "not desperate sellers."
- Treasury = "patient capital," will ride out the yield curve (no forced sales despite MTM losses).

management_tone.title: Management tone
management_tone.body: Confident and reform-minded; multiple analysts congratulated mgmt for "finally" shutting unviable OTTplay & Radio frequencies ("better late than never"). CFO upbeat on print pricing ("played out beautifully"), candid that OTTplay "didn't work" despite Tier-2/3 distribution strategy and telco competition. Repeatedly deflected forward guidance. Defensive on cash return.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- brand: Hindustan Times is India's #1 English newspaper in Delhi — evidence: ranked #1 Hindustan Times in Delhi per Average Issue Readership, IRS Q4 2019
- brand: Mint is a leading business newspaper — evidence: ranked #2 Mint, Business newspaper in India per IRS Q4 2019 — against it: ranking data is from IRS Q4 2019, not a current source

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- Newsprint cost inflation + INR depreciation squeezing print margin.
- Ad-yield sustainability vs competitive reaction (pricing not guaranteed structural).
- Radio sector "under a lot of pressure" structurally; remaining stations need profit growth.
- Treasury MTM exposure to rising bond yields (already −INR 50 cr other income hit).
- Statutory/labour-code provisions could bring further exceptional items.
- Large cash pile with no return policy = capital-allocation / value-trap concern raised by analysts.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious points
non_obvious.body:
- HMVL "other operating income" spike (~+100% YoY, ~INR 32 cr) is **AFE forfeiture** revenue — non-recurring quality of earnings flag.
- Other income drop (−INR 50 cr) is **MTM treasury losses**, not operational — should reverse if yields fall.
- OTTplay intersegment reversal restated HMVL PY print revenue down INR 6 cr (accounting, non-operational).
- Group's real digital growth vehicle is **Digicontent Ltd**, sitting *outside* the listed HT Media consol — optionality not visible in HTML numbers.
- Assetvault/AasaanWill is an unrelated-looking estate/will-planning AFE bet (8+ yrs, ~nil revenue) — speculative.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Preferential issue] Timing and approvals: approved by the Board "last month" relative to this 05-Aug-2026 filing, and still "subject to regulatory and shareholder approval" — i.e. not yet effective.
- [Comparability] "Prior period figures have been reclassified to confirm with current period, if and where ever applicable", so prior-period comparatives in the deck are restated rather than as-originally-reported.

thesis: Q4/FY26 marked a "decisive transformation" toward profitability over revenue growth: consolidated revenue flat YoY but EBITDA margin +100 bps both for quarter and full year, driven almost entirely by **Print ad-yield (pricing) gains** in English and Hindi mastheads. Management has deliberately cleaned up the loss-making portfolio — **discontinued OTTplay** (Digital) and **surrendered 6 loss-making Radio frequencies** — and says no further closure/exceptional losses are expected (ex-statutory labour-code items). Net cash remains robust, north of INR 1,000 cr; no capital return planned — cash earmarked for "businesses of tomorrow" (core print copies + Digital/Digicontent).
scorecard (consolidated, q4 fy26; fy26 f:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | INR 558 cr | **−2%** | FY26 flat YoY |
| EBITDA | INR 131 cr | **+5%** | FY26 INR 298 cr, +8% |
| EBITDA margin | 23% | +100 bps | FY26 margin also +100 bps |
| PAT (reported) | INR 96 cr | — | margin 17%; FY26 PAT INR 153 cr (margin ~8%) |
| Net cash / treasury | >INR 1,000 cr | robust | "patient capital"; MTM hit from rising yields |

**Segment revenue / op-EBITDA (Q4 FY26):**
- **Print** (consol): op revenue INR 427 cr; op-EBITDA INR 97 cr (23% margin). Ad rev INR 313 cr (+10%); circulation INR 51 cr (+4%). *FY26:* op rev INR 1,500 cr (+8%); op-EBITDA INR 208 cr (14% margin); ad rev INR 1,148 cr (+8%).
  - *Print English:* Q4 ad rev INR 172 cr (+9%); circ INR 13 cr (+13%). FY26 ad rev INR 644 cr (+8%); circ INR 53 cr (−5%).
  - *Print Hindi (HMVL):* Q4 ad rev INR 142 cr (+12%); circ INR 38 cr (flat). FY26 ad rev INR 504 cr (+8%); circ INR 155 cr (flat).
- **Radio:** Q4 op rev INR 43 cr; op-EBITDA **−INR 7 cr**. FY26 op rev INR 140 cr; op-EBITDA **−INR 22 cr**. Revenue declined on high prior-year event-led base + industry pressure.
- **Digital** (Shine + Mosaic, restated for continuing ops, ex-OTTplay): Q4 op rev INR 39 cr (flat); op-EBITDA **−INR 2 cr**. FY26 op rev INR 155 cr (flat); op-EBITDA **−INR 8 cr** (−5% margin).

**One-offs / exceptional items (FY26):** Exceptional loss from continuing ops INR 114 cr + loss from discontinued ops INR 101 cr = **INR 215 cr total** (per analyst, mgmt confirmed magnitude). A large exceptional item is provision consequent to the **new labour codes**. Other income fell INR 50 cr (INR 218 cr FY25 → INR 168 cr FY26) due to **MTM losses on treasury** as bond yields spiked (10Y ~7%). HMVL "other operating income" jumped (~INR 32 cr, ~doubled YoY) due to **AFE contract forfeiture** revenue. HMVL prior-year print segment revenue restated down ~INR 6 cr (INR 673→667 cr) — reversal of OTTplay intersegment ad spend now in discontinued ops.

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.

hero.oneLiner: A century-old Indian media group anchored in trusted Print mastheads (Hindustan Times, Hindustan, Mint), with a Radio portfolio (Fever FM, Punjabi Fever, Radio Nasha) and a Digital business centred on Shine's recruitment and upskilling offering.
